newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan bourse to computerise trading in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan bourse to computerise trading in 1997.

text.p: The Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE), Pakistan's premier bourse, expects trading volume to triple after a new computerised trading and settlement system becomes operational by May 1997.
"We expect the volume easily to go up by at least three times from its current average," Nasir Shah Bukhari, chief executive of KASB & Co brokerage house, says.
Until KSE board elections earlier this month, Bukhari was a KSE director heading a committee overseeing the proposed $1 million computerised trading system (CTS) project.
He said a central depository system (CDS) would be installed soon after the start of computerised trading, bringing about further improvement in the trading and settlement system.
"A pilot CTS was launched four months back while the stage is set for commencement of operations of the CDS," he said.

The sponsors of the $3.5 million CDS project are the Karachi, Islamabad and Lahore stock exchanges, the International Finance Corporation, Citibank, Muslim Commercial Bank, Habib Bank Ltd, National Investment Trust, Investment Corp of Pakistan and Pakistan Industrial Credit and Investment Corp.
Bukhari said the KSE will switch to a three-day settlement period once both systems are in place, instead of the current seven-day period.
"Together the whole modernisation effort will result in speedy, efficient and transparent trading and settlement of shares, and cut back on the problem of fake shares and cases of forgery," he said.

Bukhari said the need for modernisation was felt in 1991/92 when foreign funds started to show interest in Pakistani securities and the membership of brokerage houses with professional brokers and analysts began to increase.
"The KSE should set itself up to their (investors') standard and facilitate investment and trading," he said.
He said the open outcry system would not disappear and members would be allowed to trade through either system.
"Introduction of the CTS and CDS will make Pakistan more attractive to foreign investors as they will be able to deal without the hassles of physical handling of shares, he said.
